tasks.subject: Task 1: Chords
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `dsp/chords.c` knows the 26 chord types (names, tones by degree, implied scale), names chords, and recognises a chord from held notes, all pinned by host tests.

**Files:**
- Create: `firmware/src/dsp/chords.h`, `firmware/src/dsp/chords.c`, `tests/host/chords_test.c`
- Modify: `tests/run_tests.sh` (add the test), `tools/build.py` (`O2_UNITS` += `"dsp/chords.c"`), `host/build_host.sh` and `web/emu/build.sh` (add the source)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] 26 types exactly as the QY70 (manual p.41): M, add9, M7, M7(9), 6, aug, 7, 7(9), 7(#9), 7(b9), 7(13), 7(b13), 7(#11), 7(#5), 7sus4, sus4, m, madd9, m7, m7(9), m7(11), m6, mM7, m7(b5), dim, and "---" (none)
- [ ] `chord_name` gives e.g. `"C"`, `"Am7"`, `"F#7(b9)"`, `"Bm7/E"`, `"G---"` is `"G"` with no type, slash only when bass ≠ root
- [ ] recognition: every type in every root position and inversion of its 3- or 4-note core is recognised; a note below the chord's notes by more than... (see test) becomes the slash bass; one or two notes give no chord
- [ ] the test prints `chords test passed`

**Verify:** `cc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Ifirmware/src/dsp -o build/host/chords_test tests/host/chords_test.c firmware/src/dsp/chords.c && build/host/chords_test` → `... chords test passed`

tasks.subject: Task 2: The transposer
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `dsp/xpose.c` maps a pattern note written over CM7 to the current chord for each of the five track types, with limits and high key, pinned by host tests.

**Files:**
- Create: `firmware/src/dsp/xpose.h`, `firmware/src/dsp/xpose.c`, `tests/host/xpose_test.c`
- Modify: `tests/run_tests.sh`, `tools/build.py`, `host/build_host.sh`, `web/emu/build.sh`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Bypass returns the note unchanged for every chord
- [ ] Parallel: C4 E4 G4 over Am → A4 C#5 E5 (shifted +9)
- [ ] Chord 1: the CM7 voicing C4 E4 G4 B4 over Am7 → A4 C5 E5 G5; over G7 → G4 B4 D5 F5; over Dm → D4 F4 A4 D5 (the 7th folds to the octave)
- [ ] Chord 1 scale tones: D4 (the 9th) over Am7 → B4; F4 (the 11th) over G7 → C5
- [ ] Chord 2: after playing E4, the same note over A (its 3rd, C#) comes out C#4 (nearest E4), where Chord 1 gives C#5
- [ ] Bass: the first note after a chord change is the root (or the slash bass): any note → the target bass in the octave nearest the Chord 1 result; later notes follow Chord 1
- [ ] limits: a result above `hi` drops by octaves until ≤ hi; below `lo` rises; high key 5 (F): over G (root 7 > 5) the line shifts down an octave
- [ ] the test prints `xpose test passed`

**Verify:** `cc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Ifirmware/src/dsp -o build/host/xpose_test tests/host/xpose_test.c firmware/src/dsp/xpose.c firmware/src/dsp/chords.c && build/host/xpose_test` → `... xpose test passed`

tasks.subject: Task 4: The engine: playing a pattern over a chord
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `dsp/arr.c` plays a pattern's 8 tracks through the transposer over the current chord, on time, into the GM synth and MIDI out.

**Files:**
- Modify: `firmware/src/dsp/arr.h` (the engine API), `firmware/src/dsp/gm.c` (a hook to tick the arranger inside the render), `tools/build.py`, `host/build_host.sh`, `web/emu/build.sh`, `firmware/src/app/main_fm1.c` (call `arr_init`)
- Create: `firmware/src/dsp/arr.c`, `tests/host/arr_test.c`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `arr_play(1)` starts at tick 0; at 120 BPM a note at tick 24 sounds 0.5 s ± 3 ms later (the render is split at tick boundaries)
- [ ] a Chord 1 track's C4 sounds as A4 while the chord is Am7 (`gm` receives note 69 on the track's channel)
- [ ] notes end after their length (a note-off for each note-on, on the same note number, even across a chord change)
- [ ] at a chord change, a Chord 1/2/Bass note with more than 12 ticks left is cut and restruck on its new pitch; shorter ones are left to end
- [ ] mute: a muted track sends nothing; unmuting mid-pattern plays from the next note
- [ ] MIDI out: every note to the track's channel when MIDI out is on (`lf_midi_out`-style callback `arr_midi_out`)
- [ ] MIDI clock in drives the tick when present (24 a quarter), as Life's (`lf_clock`); on its own clock with MIDI out on, it sends F8 24 a quarter, FA at start, FC at stop
- [ ] `arr_test` prints `arr test passed`

**Verify:** `sh tests/run_tests.sh | grep -E "arr|all tests"` → `ok   arr` and `all tests passed`

tasks.subject: Task 5: Sections, songs, templates and live chords
tasks.description:

**Files:**

- [ ] a Fill plays one bar then goes to the other Main (from A to B, from B to A)
- [ ] an Ending plays its pattern once, then stops (`arr_playing` 0, all notes off)
- [ ] a song plays its chord track (a chord per beat; "no change" keeps the last) and its section track; it stops at its last bar unless looping
- [ ] the 16 templates (spec list) exist as chord-per-beat progressions in C; `arr_template(i)` plays one looping, transposed by the Key setting
- [ ] live chords: `arr_keys_held(notes, n)` recognises (chords.c) and sets the chord; releasing keeps it (fingered mode)

tasks.subject: Task 6: Loop recording
tasks.description:
**Goal:** REC records the keys into the selected track while the pattern loops (overdub), quantised; the track can be erased.

**Files:**
- Modify: `firmware/src/dsp/arr.c`, `arr.h`, `tests/host/arr_test.c`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `arr_record(trk, on)`; `arr_key(note, on, vel)` while recording writes a note into the playing pattern's track with its start quantised to the setting (1/16 default: 6 ticks; 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16T, 1/32, off) and its length from its release (at least one quantum)
- [ ] notes are stored *untransposed relative to the current chord*: played over Am7, a key A4 is stored as the pattern note that Chord 1 maps to A4 under Am7 (C4): the inverse of the transposer for chord tones; Bypass tracks store the key as played
- [ ] overdub: the second pass adds to the first; the pattern is full at `ARR_NEV`: further notes are dropped and `arr_full` is set
- [ ] `arr_erase_track(trk)` removes the track's notes
- [ ] recorded notes play back on the next pass

**Verify:** `sh tests/run_tests.sh | grep -E "arr|all tests"` → `ok   arr`, `all tests passed`

- [ ] the Groove MIDI Dataset's licence is read at its source (magenta.tensorflow.org/datasets/groove, the download's LICENSE): if CC BY 4.0, credit text is added to `LICENSING.md` and the README; if not CC BY (or compatible), drums are written by hand in the `.sty` format instead and the dataset is not used (record which in `styles/README.md`)
- [ ] `.sty` format (documented in `styles/README.md`): per section (`[main a]`, `[main b]`, `[fill]`, `[ending]`): `bars`, `beats`; per track: `track c1 type=chord1 program=0 lo=48 hi=84` then lines of `bar.beat.tick note length velocity` (notes as names over C M7: `C4 E4 G4`, drums as GM names `kick`, `snare`, `chh`...), or `drums from=<path to a .mid> bars=2` to take a drum loop from a MIDI file (channel 10, quantised to 24 PPQ)
- [ ] `python3 tools/make_styles.py styles/*.sty > firmware/src/dsp/styles.h` produces const `pattern_t`-shaped tables (events + track headers) and a name table; `make_styles.py --check` fails on overlong patterns (> `ARR_NEV`) and on notes outside 0..127
- [ ] the two styles play on the device (Task 11 adds 14 more); a scenario selects factory style 1 for a song and plays it: `expect notes_out >20` in 4 bars

tasks.subject: Task 4b: Sample-accurate note starts
tasks.description:
### Task 4b: Sample-accurate note starts

**Goal:** Every note the arranger starts begins on its exact sample (±1 at 22.05 kHz), not at the next 128-frame EAS block, with the synth's sound unchanged.

**Files:**
- Modify: `firmware/src/dsp/eas/eas_wtsynth.c`, `eas_wtengine.c` (and their headers / `eas_voicemgt.c` as needed): a per-voice start offset in samples within the current block; `firmware/src/dsp/gm.c` / `gm.h` (`gm_midi_now` takes an offset); `firmware/src/dsp/arr.c` (passes each note's offset into its block); `tests/host/arr_test.c`; `LICENSING.md` (Sonivox row: "modified: per-voice start offset")

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A note due at sample k of a block (0 <= k < 128 at 22.05 kHz) is silent for samples 0..k-1 of that block and starts at k: a test renders the real synth (not the stub) and finds the first non-silent output sample of an isolated note within ±1 sample (22.05 kHz) of its due time, for several k across the block and for several tempos
- [ ] Envelopes, LFOs, levels unchanged: an isolated note started at k = 0 renders bit-identically to the unmodified engine (compare against a render taken before the change)
- [ ] Note-offs may stay block-quantised (release timing), documented
- [ ] The arranger's timing tests tighten to ±1 frame at 22.05 kHz (±2 at 44.1 kHz)
- [ ] CPU: no measurable increase on the host render benchmark (<5%)

**Verify:** `sh tests/run_tests.sh | tail -1` → `all tests passed`
